notes_for_review: A local-first security analyzer paper that only cites MIT's weight-space programming as a future rung (rung 4) of an intervention ladder; no weight edit or replication has been run. Its relevance to the review is the governance stance that a weight edit must beat cheaper prompt and LoRA interventions on identical items, and that a replication of the published 0.8B edit is planned but not started. Evidence is from a small synthetic corpus with paired McNemar tests; the authors openly report that their own headline 57% figure is non-reproducible.
